cues.en: What's the connection between a dripping faucet, the Mandelbrot set, a population of rabbits, thermal convection in a fluid, and the firing of neurons in your brain? It's this one simple equation. This video is sponsored by Fast Hosts, who are offering UK viewers the chance to win a trip to South by Southwest if they can answer my question at the end of this video, so stay tuned for that. Let's say you want to model a population of rabbits.
cues.zh: 滴水的水龙头、Mandelbrot 集合、兔子种群、流体热对流，还有你大脑中神经元的放电，它们之间有什么联系？答案就是这个简单的方程。本期视频由 Fast Hosts 赞助，英国观众只要回答出片尾的问题，就有机会赢取 South by Southwest 之旅，敬请期待。假设我们想为兔子的种群数量建模。

cues.en: If you have x rabbits this year, how many rabbits will you have next year? Well, the simplest model I can imagine is where we just multiply by some number, the growth rate r, which could be, say, 2, and this would mean the population would double every year.
cues.zh: 如果今年有 x 只兔子，明年会有多少只？我想到的最简单模型，就是直接乘以一个数值——增长率 r，比如设为 2，这就意味着数量每年都会翻倍。

cues.en: And the problem with that is it means the number of rabbits would grow exponentially forever. So I can add the term 1 minus x to represent the constraints of the environment. And here I'm imagining the population x is a percentage of the theoretical maximum. So it goes from 0 to 1. And as it approaches that maximum, then this term goes to 0. And that constrains the population. So this is the logistic map.
cues.zh: 但问题在于，这意味着兔子数量会永远呈指数级增长。所以我们可以加入 (1 - x) 这一项来表示环境的承载上限。在这里，我把数量 x 设为理论最大值的比例，取值在 0 到 1 之间。随着它逼近最大值，这一项就会趋近于 0，从而限制了种群增长。这就是 Logistic 映射。

cues.en: Xn plus 1 is the population next year and Xn is the population this year. And if you graph the population next year versus the population this year, you see it is just an inverted parabola. It's the simplest equation you can make that has a negative feedback loop. The bigger the population gets over here, the smaller it'll be the following year. So let's try an example.
cues.zh: Xn+1 是明年的种群数量，Xn 是今年的数量。如果把明年的数量和今年的数量画成图表，你会发现它就是一条开口向下的抛物线。这是你能写出的包含负反馈循环的最简单方程。只要这里的种群数量变得过大，来年的数量就会减少。下面我们来看一个例子。

cues.en: Let's say we're dealing with a particularly active group of rabbits so r equals 2.6 and then let's pick a starting population of 40% of the maximum so 0.4 and then times 1 minus 0.4 and we get 0.624
cues.zh: 假设我们面对一群特别活跃的兔子，所以r等于2.6，然后我们选一个初始种群，为最大值的40%，也就是0.4，再乘以1减0.4，得到0.624

cues.en: Okay, so the population increased in the first year. But what we're really interested in is the long-term behavior of this population. So we can put this population back into the equation. And to speed things up, you can actually type 2.6 times answer times 1 minus answer, get 0.61. So the population dropped a little. Hit it again, 0.619, 0.613.
cues.zh: 好，所以第一年种群数量增加了。但我们真正关心的是这个种群的长期行为。所以我们可以把这个种群数量代回方程。为了加快速度，你可以直接输入2.6乘以答案乘以1减答案，得到0.61。所以种群数量略有下降。再按一次，0.619，0.613。

cues.en: 0.617, 0.615, 0.616, 0.615. And if I keep hitting enter here, you see that the population doesn't really change. It has stabilized, which matches what we see in the wild. Populations often remain the same as long as births and deaths are balanced. Now, I want to make a graph of this iteration. You can see here that it's reached an equilibrium value of 0.615. Now, what would happen if I changed the initial population?
cues.zh: 0.617，0.615，0.616，0.615。如果我继续按回车，你会看到种群数量并没有真正变化。它已经稳定下来了，这与我们在野外看到的情况相符。只要出生和死亡保持平衡，种群数量通常保持不变。现在，我想画一张这个迭代的图。你可以看到这里它达到了0.615的平衡值。现在，如果我改变初始种群会怎样？

cues.en: I'm just going to move this slider here and what you see is the first few years change, but the equilibrium population remains the same. So we can basically ignore the initial population. So what I'm really interested in is how does this equilibrium population vary depending on r, the growth rate? Well as you can see if I lower the growth rate, the equilibrium population decreases.
cues.zh: 我把这个滑块移到这里，你会看到前几年有变化，但平衡种群保持不变。所以我们基本上可以忽略初始种群。所以我真正感兴趣的是，这个平衡种群如何随r，即增长率，而变化？嗯，如你所见，如果我降低增长率，平衡种群会减少。

cues.en: That makes sense. And in fact, if r goes below 1, well then the population drops and eventually goes extinct. So what I want to do is make another graph where on the x-axis I have r, the growth rate, and on the y-axis I'm plotting the equilibrium population, the population you get after many many many generations.
cues.zh: 这很合理。实际上，如果 r 小于 1，种群数量就会下降并最终灭绝。所以我想画另一张图：横轴是增长率 r，纵轴表示平衡种群数量，也就是繁衍极多代之后最终达到的数量。

cues.en: Okay, for low values of r, we see the populations always go extinct, so the equilibrium value is zero. But once r hits one, the population stabilizes onto a constant value. And the higher r is, the higher the equilibrium population. So far, so good. But now comes the weird part. Once r passes three, the graph splits in two. Why? What's happening? Well, no matter how many times you iterate the equation,
cues.zh: 好，当 r 的取值较低时，种群总是会走向灭绝，所以平衡值是零。但一旦 r 达到 1，种群数量就会稳定在一个恒定值。r 越高，平衡种群数量就越大。到目前为止一切正常。但奇怪的来了：一旦 r 超过 3，图像就一分为二了。为什么？发生了什么？因为无论把这个方程迭代多少次，

cues.en: it never settles onto a single constant value. Instead, it oscillates back and forth between two values. One year the population is higher, the next year lower, and then the cycle repeats. The cyclic nature of populations is observed in nature too. One year there might be more rabbits, and then fewer the next year, and more again the year after. As R continues to increase, the fork spreads apart, and then each one splits again.
cues.zh: 它都再也不会稳定在一个恒定值上。相反，它会在两个值之间来回震荡。一年种群数量较多，下一年变少，然后循环往复。种群的周期性在自然界中也能观察到。比如某一年兔子可能很多，下一年变少，再下一年又变多。随着 R 继续增大，分叉越拉越开，接着每一支又再次分裂。

cues.en: Now, instead of oscillating back and forth between two values, populations go through a four year cycle before repeating. Since the length of the cycle, or period, has doubled, these are known as period doubling bifurcations. And as R increases further, there are more period doubling bifurcations. They come faster and faster, leading to cycles of 8, 16, 32, 64, and then at R equals 3.57, chaos.
cues.zh: 现在，种群不再是在两个值之间来回震荡，而是进入一个 4 年周期才重复一次。由于循环的长度（即周期）翻了一倍，这被称为“倍周期分岔”。随着 R 进一步增大，会出现更多的倍周期分岔。它们出现得越来越快，导致周期变为 8、16、32、64，然后在 R 等于 3.57 时，混沌出现了。

cues.en: The population never settles down at all. It bounces around as if at random. In fact, this equation provided one of the first methods of generating random numbers on computers. It was a way to get something unpredictable from a deterministic machine. There is no pattern here, no repeating. Of course, if you did know the exact initial conditions, you could calculate the values exactly. So they are considered only pseudo-random numbers.
cues.zh: 种群数量根本稳定不下来。它看起来就像在随机乱跳。实际上，这个方程提供了在计算机上生成随机数的最早方法之一。这是一种从确定性机器中获取不可预测结果的途径。这里毫无规律，也不会重复。当然，如果你确切知道初始条件，就能精确算出这些数值。所以它们只能算是伪随机数。

cues.en: Now, you might expect the equation to be chaotic from here on out, but as R increases, order returns. There are these windows of stable periodic behavior amid the chaos. For example, at R equals 3.83, there is a stable cycle with a period of 3 years. And as R continues to increase, it splits into 6, 12, 24, and so on before returning to chaos. In fact, this one equation contains periods of every length.
cues.zh: 现在，你可能会以为方程从这里开始就彻底陷入混沌了，但随着 R 的增加，秩序又回来了。在混沌之中，存在着呈现稳定周期行为的窗口。比如，在 R 等于 3.83 时，会出现一个周期为 3 年的稳定循环。随着 R 继续增大，周期又会分裂成 6、12、24 等等，然后重新归于混沌。事实上，仅这一个方程就包含了任意长度的周期。

cues.en: 37, 51, 1,052, whatever you like if you just have the right value of R. Looking at this bifurcation diagram, you may notice that it looks like a fractal. The large-scale features look to be repeated on smaller and smaller scales. And sure enough, if you zoom in, you see that it is, in fact, a fractal. Arguably the most famous fractal is the Mandelbrot set. The plot twist here...
cues.zh: 37、51、1052，只要选对 R 的取值，你想要多长都行。观察这个分岔图，你可能会发现它看起来像个分形。大尺度上的特征似乎在越来越小的尺度上不断重现。果不其然，如果放大来看，它确实就是一个分形。要说最著名的分形，大概非 Mandelbrot 集莫属了。而这里最戏剧性的反转在于……

cues.en: is that the bifurcation diagram is actually part of the Mandelbrot set. How does that work? Well, quick recap on the Mandelbrot set. It is based on this iterated equation. So the way it works is you pick a number c, any number in the complex plane, and then start with z equals 0, and then iterate this equation over and over again. If it blows up to infinity, well then the number c is not part of the set.
cues.zh: 分岔图实际上就是 Mandelbrot 集的一部分。这是怎么一回事呢？我们快速回顾一下 Mandelbrot 集。它是基于这个迭代方程构建的。它的运作方式是：在复平面上任选一个数 c，以 z 等于 0 作为起始值，然后一遍又一遍地迭代这个方程。如果计算结果发散到了无穷大，那么数 c 就不属于该集合。

cues.en: But if this number remains finite after unlimited iterations, well then it is part of the Mandelbrot set. So let's try for example C equals 1. So we've got 0 squared plus 1 equals 1, then 1 squared plus 1 equals 2, 2 squared plus 1 equals 5, 5 squared plus 1 equals 26. So pretty quickly you can see that with C equals 1, this equation is going to blow up. So
cues.zh: 但如果这个数值在无限次迭代后仍然有限，那它就属于曼德博集合。那我们试试 C 等于 1。于是有 0 的平方加 1 等于 1，然后 1 的平方加 1 等于 2，2 的平方加 1 等于 5，5 的平方加 1 等于 26。所以很快你就能看出，当 C 等于 1 时，这个方程会发散。所以

cues.en: The number one is not part of the Mandelbrot set. What if we try c equals negative one? Well, then we've got zero squared minus one equals negative one. Negative one squared minus one equals zero. And so we're back to zero squared minus one equals negative one. So we see that this function is going to keep oscillating back and forth between negative one and zero. And so it'll remain finite. And so c equals negative one is part of the Mandelbrot set.
cues.zh: 数字 1 不属于曼德博集合。那试试 c 等于 -1 呢？那么有 0 的平方减 1 等于 -1。-1 的平方减 1 等于 0。于是又回到 0 的平方减 1 等于 -1。所以我们看到这个函数会在 -1 和 0 之间来回振荡。因此它会保持有限。所以 c 等于 -1 属于曼德博集合。

cues.en: Now normally when you see pictures of the Mandelbrot set, it just shows you the boundary between the numbers that cause this iterated equation to remain finite and those that cause it to blow up. But it doesn't really show you how these numbers stay finite. So what we've done here is actually iterated that equation thousands of times and then plotted on the z-axis the value that that iteration actually takes.
cues.zh: 通常你看到曼德博集合的图片时，它只展示了让这个迭代方程保持有限的数与让它发散的数之间的边界。但它并没有真正展示这些数是如何保持有限的。所以我们在这里做的是，实际上把这个方程迭代了数千次，然后在 z 轴上画出该迭代实际取到的值。

cues.en: So if we look from the side, what you'll actually see is the bifurcation diagram. It is part of this Mandelbrot set. So what's really going on here? Well, what this is showing us is that all of the numbers in the main cardioid, they end up stabilizing onto a single constant value. But the numbers in this main bulb
cues.zh: 所以如果从侧面看，你实际看到的是分岔图。它是这个曼德博集合的一部分。那这里到底发生了什么？它告诉我们的是，主心形内所有的数最终都会稳定到一个单一的常数值。但在这个主球泡内的数

cues.en: well, they end up oscillating back and forth between two values. And in this bulb, they end up oscillating between four values. They've got a period of four, and then eight, and then 16, 32, and so on. And then you hit the chaotic part. The chaotic part of the bifurcation diagram happens out here on what's called the needle of the Mandelbrot set, where the Mandelbrot set gets really thin.
cues.zh: 它们最终会在两个值之间来回振荡。而在这个球泡里，它们最终会在四个值之间振荡。它们的周期是四，然后是八，再是 16、32，以此类推。然后你就进入了混沌部分。分岔图的混沌部分出现在这里，位于所谓的曼德博集合的针状区域，那里曼德博集合变得非常细。

cues.en: And you can see this medallion here that looks like a smaller version of the entire Mandelbrot set, well that corresponds to the window of stability in the bifurcation plot with a period of three. Now the bifurcation diagram only exists on the real line because we only put real numbers into our equation. But all of these bulbs off of the main cardioid, well, they also have periodic cycles.
cues.zh: 你看这个像整个曼德博集合缩小版的圆形图案，它对应分岔图中周期为三的稳定窗口。分岔图只存在于实轴上，因为我们只把实数代入方程。但主心形上的所有这些球状结构，也都有周期循环。

cues.en: of, for example, three or four or five. And so you see these repeated ghostly images if we look in the z-axis. Effectively, they're oscillating between these values as well. Personally, I find this extraordinarily beautiful. But if you're more practically minded, you may be asking, but does this equation actually model populations of animals? And the answer is yes.
cues.zh: 比如三、四或五的周期。所以如果沿z轴观察，你会看到这些重复的幽灵般的图像。实际上，它们也在这些值之间振荡。我个人觉得这极其美丽。但如果你更注重实际，可能会问，这个方程真的能模拟动物种群吗？答案是肯定的。

cues.en: particularly in the controlled environment scientists have set up in labs. What I find even more amazing is how this one simple equation applies to a huge range of totally unrelated areas of science. The first major experimental confirmation came from a fluid dynamicist named Libchaber. He created a small rectangular box with mercury inside and he used a small temperature gradient to induce convection. Just
cues.zh: 尤其是在科学家在实验室里建立的受控环境中。我觉得更神奇的是，这个简单的方程如何适用于科学中大量完全不相关的领域。第一个重要的实验验证来自一位名叫Libchaber的流体动力学家。他制作了一个内部装有水银的小矩形盒，并用小温度梯度引发对流。只是

cues.en: two counter-rotating cylinders of fluid inside his box. That's all the box was large enough for. And of course he couldn't look in and see what the fluid was doing, so he measured the temperature using a probe in the top. And what he saw was a regular spike, a periodic spike in the temperature. That's like when the logistic equation converges on a single value.
cues.zh: 盒子里有两圈反向旋转的流体圆柱。盒子就只够容纳这么多。当然，他无法看进去观察流体在做什么，所以用顶部的一个探针测量温度。他看到的是规则的尖峰，温度中的周期性尖峰。这就像逻辑斯蒂方程收敛到单一值时的情形。

cues.en: But as he increased the temperature gradient, a wobble developed on those rolling cylinders at half the original frequency. The spikes in temperature were no longer the same height. Instead, they went back and forth between two different heights. He had achieved period two. And as he continued to increase the temperature, he saw period doubling again. Now he had four different temperatures before the cycle repeated. And then eight.
cues.zh: 但随着他增大温度梯度，那些滚动圆柱上出现了摆动，频率变成了原来的一半。温度峰值的高度也不再相同。相反，它们在两种不同的高度之间来回变化。他实现了二倍周期。随着他继续升高温度，他又看到了周期倍增。现在，循环重复前会经历四种不同的温度。接着是八种。

cues.en: This was a pretty spectacular confirmation of the theory in a beautifully crafted experiment. But this was only the beginning. Scientists have studied the response of our eyes and salamander eyes to flickering lights. And what they find is a period doubling. That once the light reaches a certain rate of flickering, our eyes only respond to every other flicker.
cues.zh: 这是对该理论相当精彩的验证，实验设计也十分精巧。但这还只是开始。科学家研究了人眼和蝾螈眼睛对闪烁光的响应。他们发现了周期倍增现象：当光线的闪烁达到一定频率后，我们的眼睛只会对每隔一次的闪烁作出响应。

cues.en: It's amazing in these papers to see the bifurcation diagram emerge, albeit a bit fuzzy because it comes from real world data. In another study, scientists gave rabbits a drug that sent their hearts into fibrillation. I guess they felt there were too many rabbits out there. I mean, if you don't know what fibrillation is, it's where your heart beats in an incredibly irregular way and doesn't really pump any blood. So if you don't fix it, you die. But what they found was
cues.zh: 在这些论文中看到分岔图逐渐显现，真是令人惊叹，尽管由于数据来自现实世界，图像有些模糊。在另一项研究中，科学家给兔子注射了一种会让心脏发生颤动的药物。我猜是因为他们觉得兔子太多了。我的意思是，如果你不知道什么是心室颤动，它指的是心脏以极不规则的方式跳动，基本无法泵出血液。所以如果不及时纠正，就会死亡。但他们发现，

cues.en: On the path to Fibrillation, they found the period doubling route to Chaos. The rabbit started out with a periodic beat, and then it went into a two cycle, two beats close together, and then a four cycle, four different beats before it repeated again, and eventually a periodic behavior.
cues.zh: 在走向心室颤动的过程中，兔子经历了通往混沌的周期倍增路线。兔子一开始是周期性跳动，随后进入二周期，也就是两个彼此接近的心跳；接着是四周期，重复前会出现四种不同的心跳，最终又回到了周期性行为。

cues.en: Now, what was really cool about this study was they monitored the heart in real time and used chaos theory to determine when to apply electrical shocks to the heart to return it to periodicity. And they were able to do that successfully. So they used chaos to control a heart and figure out a smarter way to deliver electric shocks to set it beating normally again. That's pretty amazing.
cues.zh: 这项研究真正酷的地方在于，他们实时监测心脏，并利用混沌理论来确定何时对心脏施加电击，使其恢复周期性。他们成功地做到了这一点。所以，他们利用混沌来控制心脏，找到了一种更智能的电击方式，让心脏重新正常跳动。这真是太神奇了。

cues.en: And then there is the issue of the dripping faucet. Most of us, of course, think of dripping faucets as very regular periodic objects. But a lot of research has gone into finding that once the flow rate increases a little bit, you get period doubling. So now the drips come two at a time. And eventually, from a dripping faucet, you can get chaotic behavior just by adjusting the flow rate.
cues.zh: 然后还有滴水龙头的问题。我们大多数人当然认为滴水龙头是非常规律、周期性的物体。但大量研究表明，一旦流速稍微增加，就会出现倍周期现象。所以现在水滴一次滴两滴。最终，仅仅通过调节流速，滴水龙头就能产生混沌行为。

cues.en: And you think, like, what really is a faucet? Well, there's constant pressure water and a constant size aperture, and yet what you're getting is chaotic dripping. So this is a really easy, chaotic system you can experiment with at home. Go open a tap just a little bit and see if you can get aperiodic dripping in your house. The bifurcation diagram pops up in so many different places that it starts to feel spooky. Now I want to...
cues.zh: 你会想，水龙头到底是什么？嗯，有恒定压力的水和恒定大小的孔径，然而你得到的却是混沌的滴漏。所以这是一个非常容易的混沌系统，你可以在家做实验。稍微打开一点水龙头，看看你家里能不能出现非周期性的滴漏。分岔图出现在太多不同的地方，开始让人觉得诡异。现在我想……

cues.en: tell you something that'll make it seem even spookier. There was this physicist, Mitchell Feigenbaum, who was looking at when the bifurcations occur. He divided the width of each bifurcation section by the next one, and he found that ratio closed in on this number, 4.669, which is now called the Feigenbaum constant.
cues.zh: 告诉你一些会让它显得更诡异的事情。有一位物理学家，Mitchell Feigenbaum，他在研究分岔何时发生。他把每个分岔部分的宽度除以下一个分岔部分的宽度，发现这个比值趋近于这个数字，4.669，现在被称为Feigenbaum常数。

cues.en: The bifurcations come faster and faster, but in a ratio that approaches this fixed value. And no one knows where this constant comes from. It doesn't seem to relate to any other known physical constant. So it is itself a fundamental constant of nature. What's even crazier is that it doesn't have to be the particular form of the equation I showed you earlier. Any equation that has a single hump
cues.zh: 分岔来得越来越快，但比例趋近于这个固定值。没人知道这个常数从何而来。它似乎与任何其他已知物理常数都无关。所以它本身就是自然界的一个基本常数。更疯狂的是，它并不局限于我之前展示的那个特定形式的方程。任何具有单峰的方程

cues.en: If you iterate it the way that we have, so you could use xn plus 1 equals sin x, for example, if you iterate that one again and again and again, you will also see bifurcations. Not only that, but the ratio of when those bifurcations occur will have the same scaling, 4.669. Any single hump function iterated will give you that fundamental constant.
cues.zh: 如果你像我们这样迭代它，比如用 xn 加 1 等于 sin x，如果你反复迭代这个式子，你也会看到分岔。不仅如此，这些分岔发生时的比例也会有相同的缩放，4.669。任何单峰函数迭代都会给出这个基本常数。

cues.en: So why is this? Well, it's referred to as universality because there seems to be something fundamental and very universal about this process, this type of equation, and that constant value. In 1976, the biologist Robert May wrote a paper in Nature about this very equation. It sparked a revolution in people looking into this stuff. I mean, that paper's been cited thousands of times.
cues.zh: 那么为什么会这样呢？它被称为普适性，因为这个过程、这类方程以及那个常数值似乎有着某种根本且非常普遍的东西。1976年，生物学家 Robert May 在《Nature》上发表了一篇关于这个方程的论文。这引发了人们研究这类东西的革命。我是说，那篇论文已被引用数千次。

cues.en: And in the paper he makes this plea that we should teach students about this simple equation because it gives you a new intuition for ways in which simple things, simple equations, can create very complex behaviors. And I still think that today we don't really teach this way.
cues.zh: 在论文中，他呼吁我们应该教学生这个简单的方程，因为它能给你一种新的直觉，让你理解简单的事物、简单的方程如何能创造出非常复杂的行为。我仍然认为，今天我们并没有真正这样教。

cues.en: I mean, we teach simple equations and simple outcomes because those are the easy things to do and those are the things that make sense. We're not going to throw chaos at students, but maybe we should. Maybe we should throw at least a little bit, which is why I've been so excited about chaos and I'm so excited about this equation because, you know, how did I get to be 37 years old without hearing of the Feigenbaum constant?
cues.zh: 我的意思是，我们教简单的方程和简单的结果，因为这些是容易做的事情，也是说得通的事情。我们不会把混沌扔给学生，但也许我们应该这么做。也许我们至少应该扔一点，这就是为什么我对混沌如此兴奋，对这条方程如此兴奋，因为，你知道，我怎么活到37岁还没听说过费根鲍姆常数？
